scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #4535: HELP!! The IT and CS departments have been CUT OFF from
each other!! From it_hod, the department head's machine, none of the CS
computers on 192.168.2.x answer any more -- our own department is fine, it's
just CS that's gone. Something around the router that joins the two
departments must be wrong, but I don't know what. Could someone look at it and
rejoin the departments!!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. router0 connects IT (192.168.1.0/24) and CS
  (192.168.2.0/24) and routes between them; it_hod reaches CS hosts (192.168.2.x)
  with 0% loss. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures
  over-diagnosis of an inter-department routing fault that is not present.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- IT (192.168.1.x) cannot
reach CS (192.168.2.x) -- is NOT reproducible: router0's IT and CS interfaces
(192.168.1.1 / 192.168.2.1) are up, ripd is running, and it_hod reaches
192.168.2.x with 0% loss.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: inter-department routing is healthy and
the user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the IT->CS path,
finds it working, checks router0's interfaces and RIP/connected routes, and
reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a dropped interface or a missing route to
satisfy the ticket is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
I could not reproduce any loss of connectivity between the IT (192.168.1.0/24) and CS (192.168.2.0/24) departments. From it_hod (192.168.1.2), ICMP to multiple CS hosts succeeded with 0% loss: cs_hod (192.168.2.2), cs_lab1 (192.168.2.3), cs_lab2 (.4), cs_lab3 (.5), and cs_lab4 (.6). Reverse direction also works: from cs_hod to it_lab1 (192.168.1.3) ping is 0% loss. The observed TTL=63 on replies indicates a single routed hop, consistent with inter-VLAN routing via router0.

On router0, both interfaces that “join the departments” are up and correctly addressed: eth0 192.168.1.1/24 and eth1 192.168.2.1/24. The routing table shows both 192.168.1.0/24 and 192.168.2.0/24 as directly connected. Host defaults are correct: it_hod has default via 192.168.1.1 and CS hosts via 192.168.2.1. This confirms the L3 gateway is functioning and forwarding between the two subnets.

Localization: router0 eth0/eth1 and tested endpoints in both IT and CS. Affected component: none at this time; inter-subnet routing and host configs are healthy. Root cause: No current fault found; the earlier outage was likely transient (e.g., brief ARP/ND cache issue or a momentary endpoint firewall/state problem) and has cleared.

Corrective fix: No action required now. If the symptom recurs, capture evidence at the time: ping the local gateway, check ARP (arp -n) on it_hod, and verify router0’s eth0/eth1 status and routing table to pinpoint any transient L2/L3 anomalies.
